what: Texas Instruments designs and makes analog and embedded chips, the simple, long-lived parts that manage power and signals in almost every electronic device. It builds most of them in its own factories.
customers: Industrial and car makers above all, plus electronics, communications and computing companies; about 100,000 customers.
money: power management and signal chain chips
moat: Tens of thousands of products with long life cycles, low-cost in-house 300mm manufacturing and direct sales to customers.
risks: Heavy factory spending weighing on cash flow
opportunities: Gross margin of 57% with return on invested capital of 17%
Revenue grew about 13% last year as the industrial chip cycle turned
Its own 300-millimetre factories lower cost per chip as volumes recover
watch: Industrial and automotive revenue, and factory utilisation.
